summary.name: Claude Code
summary.one_liner: Official conceptual guide to how Claude Code works: its agentic loop of gathering context, acting with tools, and verifying results, plus its context window, sessions, and safety features.
keywords: ai edits files and runs tests
use_cases: understanding how Claude Code plans and executes coding tasks
managing long conversations and context limits
parallel work across git branches with worktrees
undoing unwanted file edits made by an AI agent
configuring permission modes for AI agent actions
summary.what_it_does: Explains the agentic loop in which Claude gathers context, takes action with tools such as file reads, edits, and shell commands, and verifies results, repeating as needed. Describes the tools Claude can use, what it can access in a project (files, terminal, git state, CLAUDE.md, auto memory, extensions), and how it runs across terminal, desktop, IDE, and CI/CD interfaces. Covers session storage as local JSONL files, resume and fork behavior, the context window and automatic compaction, and safety through file checkpoints and permission modes.
notable: Agentic loop of gather context, take action, and verify results, with user interruption at any point
Per-session context window with CLAUDE.md, auto memory, and automatic compaction
File checkpoints that let you rewind edits, separate from git
Multiple permission modes including Auto, Manual, Accept edits, and Plan
caveats: Checkpoints only cover file changes; actions on remote systems such as databases, APIs, and deployments cannot be checkpointed
Auto permission mode availability depends on Claude Code version and plan on earlier versions
Detailed instructions from early in a conversation can be lost during compaction
